messages:
meera: Quick heads-up — I'm hitting a deterministic divergence during long-prefill runs on the new onboarded model (orpheus-int4-hybrid). When prefill > ~65k tokens the later generation drifts vs fp16 baseline. Repro steps and logs below.

lee: Yikes. same cluster or local?

meera: ran on dev-gpu-12, single-shard. Command I used:

```bash
python tests/longctx_runner.py \
  --model orpheus-int4-hybrid \
  --seq 70000 \
  --prefill 66000 \
  --quant-mode hybrid3 \
  --rotary-rescale on \
  --save-trace /tmp/repro.trace
```

meera: Log excerpt (truncated):

```
[2025-06-02 09:12:34] prefill: tokens=66012
[2025-06-02 09:12:35] kv_store: kv_index=65536 mapped_shard=0 offset=0
[2025-06-02 09:12:35] kv_store: kv_index=65537 mapped_shard=0 offset=-1  <-- suspicious
[2025-06-02 09:12:36] generation: token=65550 fingerprint_mismatch
[2025-06-02 09:12:36] mismatch: baseline_fp16=0x7f3a4e, current=0x7f3642
```

sam: is this an index wrap or an off-by-one in the mapping? rotor/rope scaling change recently landed in runtime, right?

meera: yes, runtime PR #4124 changed the rotary rescale clip for longctx. But disabling rotary-rescale shifts where the mismatch shows up (later by a few hundred tokens) instead of fixing it.

carlos: could be "entropy echo" where quantization + rope scaling causes a tiny phase offset that accumulates into a token-level pivot. Also check sign-extension during memcpy for int3/packed formats.

bench-bot: quick perf snapshot:
- baseline fp16: pass (no mismatch)
- int4-hybrid (current): reproducible mismatch at ~65550
- hybrid3 (packed int3-ish): mismatch earlier ~65210

lee: can you grep for any negative offsets or sentinel values near 65536? maybe shard modulo logic breaks at power-of-two boundary.

meera: did that — found this in kv debug: `kv_meta: token=65537 -> shard_idx=0, local_idx=-1` which looks like a map/unpack bug. attaching trace shortly.

sam: try running with `--kv-wrap-mode truncate` and `--no-prefetch` to see if preventing wrap avoids the fingerprint hit. If that helps, it's almost certainly a mapping/wrap semantics problem.

meera: kicked off short runs now with: `--kv-wrap-mode truncate --no-prefetch`. also trying `--quant-mode int4 --disable-rotary-rescale` as a control.

carlos: if repro is fast enough, can you also run with `--dump-kv-headers` and paste first 128/last 128 entries? the pattern around 65536 will be telling.

meera: will do. opening an internal ticket with trace + sample binary diff. tagging @eng-runtime for kernel/packing review. :hourglass_flowing_sand:

lee: thanks — sounds like a good bisect candidate (runtime vs quant codec). ping here when you have the kv header dump.

meera: reduced repro created (still >64k prefill) and uploaded to s3://redwood-repro/longctx/1739456789.tar.gz. I'll update the ticket with the minimal C-level trace and exact command to reproduce in CI.

meera: (follow-up) quick result: `--kv-wrap-mode truncate` prevented the mismatch on 3/3 runs. so mapping/wrap logic very likely root cause. Will follow up with a small runtime patch and bench results.

sam: great, that gives us a clear mitigation path. when you open the PR add the failing testcase under tests/longctx/ so CI can catch regressions. :+1:
